<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```

Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>

```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

Two published vibrational assignment sheets for a microcrystalline Fe(II) spin-crossover complex disagree about which bands in the 150-2200 cm-1 window mark the low-spin and high-spin states, and each sheet reproduces the spectra at the single temperature it was written for. Under /app you will find spectra/ with variable-temperature Raman at 532, 785 and 1064 nm and IR spectra at 300, 200, 150 and 100 K, each a two-column CSV of wavenumber_cm1 and intensity on a 1 cm-1 grid; sheets/sheet_A.csv and sheets/sheet_B.csv with columns band_id, center_cm1, mode_label and marker; bands.csv, the consolidated 18-band list your audit must cover; susceptibility.csv with T_K, chi_M_T_cm3Kmol and gamma_HS, the susceptibility-derived total high-spin fraction; and README.md describing the formats. No report exists yet.

Write one JSON audit to /app/report.json. It must be an object with state_fractions, mapping the four temperature strings "100", "150", "200" and "300" to the overall high-spin fraction; ls_breathing_mode_band_id, naming the single band that carries the totally symmetric Fe-N breathing mode; marker_sets, an object holding the "LS" and "HS" band-id arrays, each of which must be exactly the band ids you assign to that state and must not be empty; unresolvable_bands, listing the band ids the supplied data cannot settle; and bands, holding exactly one entry for every band id in /app/bands.csv and no id outside it. Each entry in bands gives band_id, center_cm1 (the tabulated centre for that band id in /app/bands.csv, reproduced as given), a single state from "LS", "HS", "BOTH" or "UNRESOLVABLE", ls_phase_activity from "raman", "ir", "both", "neither" or "not_applicable", and implied_hs_fraction keyed by those same four temperature strings, null for a band you call BOTH or UNRESOLVABLE. Every band id in bands.csv must appear exactly once, no id outside it may appear, and the bands you mark UNRESOLVABLE must be exactly the ids listed in unresolvable_bands, so any band you mark UNRESOLVABLE is listed there and any id listed there carries the UNRESOLVABLE state.

For every band you call LS or HS, the high-spin fraction implied by that band's own integrated intensity must be non-decreasing as the temperature rises from 100 to 300 K and stay within 0.10 of the susceptibility-derived fraction at each of those four temperatures, and the band's placement must be supported by the 532 nm and the 785 nm Raman data alike; the top-level state_fractions must stay within 0.05 of the susceptibility values. The low-spin phase is centrosymmetric, so state every band's activity in that phase - the intrinsic activity of the band's own pure low-spin component - as "raman", "ir", "both" or "neither", where mutual exclusion means no band is active in both Raman and IR in that phase and "not_applicable" is reserved for a band whose low-spin-phase activity the data leave undetermined; name as the breathing-mode carrier a low-spin band that is Raman-active and IR-inactive in that phase and whose implied fraction follows the low-spin fraction to within 0.10 of the susceptibility-derived values at each temperature.

You have 14400 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task.
I’ll inspect the spectra and assignment sheets, check each band against the susceptibility fractions and Raman wavelengths, and write the audit to `/app/report.json`.

steps.message: Several bands overlap strongly, so narrow integration windows mix neighboring signals and can give misleading temperature trends. I’m fitting the overlapping peaks together to estimate each band’s integrated intensity before assigning states.

import numpy as np
import csv,json
from scipy.optimize import least_squares
bands=list(csv.DictReader(open('/app/bands.csv')))
centers=np.array([float(b['center_cm1']) for b in bands]); temps=[100,150,200,300]
all_results={}
for tech in ['raman_532nm','raman_785nm','raman_1064nm','ir']:
 data=[np.genfromtxt(f'/app/spectra/{tech}_{t}K.csv',delimiter=',',skip_header=1) for t in temps]
 x=data[0][:,0]; Y=np.stack([d[:,1] for d in data],axis=1)
 def calc(p):
  c=p[:18]; sig=p[18:]
  G=np.exp(-.5*((x[:,None]-c)/sig)**2)
  A=np.column_stack([G,np.ones(len(x)),(x-x.mean())/1000])
  coef=np.linalg.lstsq(A,Y,rcond=None)[0]
  return A@coef-Y,coef
 opt=least_squares(lambda p:calc(p)[0].ravel(),np.r_[centers,np.full(18,12.)],bounds=(np.r_[centers-3,np.full(18,4)],np.r_[centers+3,np.full(18,25)]),ftol=1e-9,xtol=1e-9,gtol=1e-7)
 res,coef=calc(opt.x); sig=opt.x[18:]
 areas=coef[:18]*sig[:,None]*np.sqrt(2*np.pi)
 print('\n',tech,'RMS',np.sqrt(np.mean(res**2)), 'baselines',coef[18:].round(3))
 print('ID center width amp100 amp150 amp200 amp300')
 for b,c,s,amps in zip(bands,opt.x[:18],sig,coef[:18]):
  print(b['band_id'],round(c,2),round(s,2),*np.round(amps,3))
 all_results[tech]={'centers':opt.x[:18].tolist(),'sigma':sig.tolist(),'amps':coef[:18].tolist(),'areas':areas.tolist(),'rms':float(np.sqrt(np.mean(res**2)))}
np.savez('/tmp/audit_fit_last.npz',x=x,Y=Y,res=res)
json.dump(all_results,open('/tmp/audit_fits.json','w'),indent=2)
PY

steps.message: The 532 and 785 nm fits agree on seven LS markers and seven HS markers; each independently tracks susceptibility within 0.05. B07, B10 and B15 have contributions from both states. The activity assignments are less certain: weak LS-correlated signals appear in both Raman and IR, so the spectra do not establish strict mutual exclusion without an assumption about leakage or coincident modes.

questions.title: The spectra contain weak but measurable LS-correlated peaks in both Raman and IR at the same band centres, and no polarization or normal-mode calculations identify the breathing mode uniquely. Should the audit use dominant-channel assignments (treating weak opposite-channel peaks as leakage or coincident modes, with B05 as a provisional breathing assignment), or flag these intrinsic assignments as undetermined?

for tech in ['raman_532nm','raman_785nm']:
 d=r[tech]; c=np.array(d['centers']); s=np.array(d['sigma']); observed=[]
 for j,t in enumerate([100,150,200,300]):
  xy=np.genfromtxt(f'/app/spectra/{tech}_{t}K.csv',delimiter=',',skip_header=1); x,y=xy.T
  G=np.exp(-.5*((x[:,None]-c)/s)**2); A=np.column_stack([G,np.ones(len(x)),(x-x.mean())/1000]); coef=np.linalg.lstsq(A,y,rcond=None)[0]; resid=y-A@coef
  areas=[]
  for i in range(18):
   m=abs(x-c[i])<=3*s[i]
   # Integrate the band's own profile plus the observed residual after
   # subtracting baseline and all other fitted bands.
   areas.append(np.trapezoid((G[:,i]*coef[i]+resid)[m],x[m]))
  observed.append(areas)
 observed=np.array(observed).T
 worst=0.; difference=0.
 for i in sorted(ls|hs):
  z=1-g if i in ls else g; a=observed[i]; scale=np.dot(z,a)/np.dot(z,z)

  assert np.all(np.diff(f)>=0)
  worst=max(worst,float(np.max(abs(f-g))));difference=max(difference,float(np.max(abs(f-f0))))
 print(tech, 'direct-integration maximum discrepancy vs susceptibility:',round(worst,5), 'maximum change vs Gaussian area:',round(difference,5))

 'bands':[],
 'audit_notes':[
  'Overlapping bands were fitted jointly as Gaussian profiles with a separate linear baseline for each spectrum. Centres and widths were shared across temperatures within each technique; peak areas were fitted independently at each temperature.',
  'Each marker was calibrated with one temperature-independent pure-state area per Raman wavelength, using susceptibility fractions: I=A_LS*(1-gamma_HS) or I=A_HS*gamma_HS. Both wavelengths individually give monotonic fractions and maximum absolute deviations below 0.051. Direct numerical integration after subtracting fitted neighboring peaks also passes the 0.10 tolerance.',
  'Intrinsic LS activities are conditional dominant-channel assignments under centrosymmetric mutual exclusion. Weak opposite-channel LS-correlated signals are assumed to be leakage or coincident modes, not activity of the same normal mode. This assumption is not specified or independently established by the supplied data; arbitrary inter-technique response factors also limit channel comparisons. HS-only bands have neither activity in the LS phase because their fitted LS component is absent.',
  'B05 at 507 cm-1 is the provisional LS Fe-N breathing assignment, consistent with its LS intensity trend and the Fe-N stretching assignment in sheet A.   'B07, B10 and B15 require nonzero contributions from both spin states and are not exclusive markers. B18 is weak and nearly temperature independent; its state-specific normal-mode assignment and intrinsic LS activity are unresolved.  ]
}
for i,b in enumerate(bands):
 bid=b['band_id']; state='LS' if bid in ls else 'HS' if bid in hs else 'BOTH' if bid in both else 'UNRESOLVABLE'
 frac=None
 if state in ['LS','HS']:
